page.layout: One photograph of a book spine, lying flat. Lettering in brown ink runs vertically across the vellum spine. Two shelf-mark labels and a digitiser caption are not part of the printed page.
page.notes: This scan shows a book spine, not a printed text page. The spine lettering is in brown ink, apparently handwritten on the vellum, so it is not transcribed as printed text. As read from the spine, left to right: "Jud. WAEYEN" (the first word partly cut off at the edge), "Sententia Reformator", "de Interpret. Script. Sacr. contra WOLZOGIUM", and "Amstel. 1669" at the far right. Some letters are faint, especially "Interpret." and "Sacr.", which I read with some doubt. Excluded as not printed: the round labels "233" and "G 1", and the digitiser caption at the bottom left ("Early European Books, Copyright © 2011 ProQuest LLC. Images reproduced by courtesy of Koninklijke Bibliotheek, Den Haag. 233 G 7").
